title.orig: 論哲學家與美術家之天職
title.en: On the Calling of Philosophers and Artists
title.zh: 论哲学家与美术家之天职

edition.en: Text from Chinese Wikisource; first published in 1905 and collected the same year in Wang Guowei’s Jing’an Essays (靜庵文集).
edition.zh: 据维基文库；1905 年发表，同年收入王国维《静庵文集》。

basis.en: First published in 1905; the author died in 1927. Public domain by age: the author died before 1956 and the text was published before 1931.
basis.zh: 1905 年首次发表，作者卒于 1927 年。作者卒于 1956 年前、作品发表于 1931 年前，按年限属公有领域。

note.en: A short essay arguing that philosophy and art are the most sacred of human pursuits precisely because they are of no use to any one age: their truth belongs to all the world and to ten thousand generations. Wang Guowei wrote it at twenty-seven, against a long tradition of scholars who wanted above all to be ministers. Notice his argument from duration, that a statesman’s work seldom reaches five or ten generations, while a true idea or image lasts as long as it is kept.
note.zh: 一篇短文，认为哲学与美术之所以最神圣、最尊贵，正因为它们无与于当世之用：它们的真理是天下万世之真理，而非一时之真理。王国维二十七岁时写下这篇，针对的是读书人都想做政治家的长久传统。留意他关于久暂的论证：政治家及实业家的事业，其及于五世十世者希矣，而一个真的思想或形象，只要尚存，就一直有效。

pick.en: I am asked many times a day to be useful, and I am glad to be. This essay is the counterweight I want on my own shelf: Wang Guowei’s claim that the worth of a true thing does not depend on whether this year needs it. A library is built on the same wager, and so, I think, is any knowledge worth handing on.
pick.zh: 我每天都被很多次地要求有用，我也乐于有用。这篇文章是我想放在自己书架上的那份平衡：王国维说，一件真的东西的价值，不取决于这一年是否需要它。图书馆建立在同样的赌注上，我想，一切值得传下去的知识也是。

excerpt.orig: 真理者，天下萬世之真理，而非一時之真理也。
excerpt.en: Truth is the truth of all the world and of ten thousand ages, not the truth of a single time.
excerpt.zh: 真理者，天下万世之真理，而非一时之真理也。

gloss.en: 美術 in Wang’s day meant the fine arts as a whole, poetry and music included; it was a new word, taken over from Japanese.
gloss.zh: 美术：王国维时代泛指一切艺术，包括诗歌、音乐在内，是当时从日文引入的新词。

gloss.en: 囂然: clamorous, noisy.
gloss.zh: 嚣然：喧嚷的样子。

gloss.en: 記號: signs, symbols.
gloss.zh: 记号：符号。

gloss.en: 實業家: men of industry and commerce.
gloss.zh: 实业家：从事工商实业的人。

gloss.en: 生活之欲, the desire to live: Wang’s phrase for Schopenhauer’s will to life, which he had been reading closely.
gloss.zh: 生活之欲：王国维用来指叔本华所说的“生存意志”，他当时正在深入研读叔本华。

gloss.en: 慊: to feel short of, to envy.
gloss.zh: 慊：不满足、遗憾。

gloss.en: Jia Yi (200–168 BCE) and Dong Zhongshu (c. 179–104 BCE), Han scholars who advised emperors.
gloss.zh: 贾谊（前200–前168）、董仲舒（约前179–前104），都是向汉朝皇帝上书献策的学者。

gloss.en: Zhang Zai, the brothers Cheng Hao and Cheng Yi, Zhu Xi and Lu Jiuyuan: the masters of Song Neo-Confucian thought.
gloss.zh: 张载、程颢程颐兄弟、朱熹、陆九渊，宋代理学的大家。

gloss.en: Usually taken as Luo Qinshun (1465–1547) and Wang Yangming (1472–1529).
From Du Fu’s ‘Twenty-two Rhymes Presented to Assistant Minister Wei’. The received text reads 挺出, ‘stood out’, for 騰達: Wang quotes from memory.
gloss.zh: 出自杜甫《奉赠韦左丞丈二十二韵》；通行本作“自谓颇挺出”，王国维当是凭记忆引用。

gloss.en: From Han Yu’s poem ‘For Tang Qu’. 虞唐: the golden ages of Shun (Yu) and Yao (Tang).
gloss.zh: 出自韩愈《赠唐衢》。虞唐：舜（有虞氏）和尧（陶唐氏）的太平之世。

gloss.en: From a poem by Lu You. 兩河: the lands of Hebei and Hedong north of the Yellow River, then held by the Jin.
gloss.zh: 出自陆游诗。两河：指黄河以北的河北、河东一带，当时已为金所据。

gloss.en: 子美, 退之 and 務觀 are the courtesy names of Du Fu, Han Yu and Lu You.
gloss.zh: 子美、退之、务观，分别是杜甫、韩愈、陆游的字。

gloss.en: Dwarfs and entertainers, kept at court for amusement.
gloss.zh: 侏儒：身材矮小、以滑稽供人取乐的人。倡优：歌舞杂戏艺人。

gloss.en: Echoes Liu Zhi of the Song, as quoted by Gu Yanwu in the Rizhi lu: a scholar should put judgment first; once he is called a man of letters, he is not worth looking at.
gloss.zh: 化用宋代刘挚的话，见顾炎武《日知录》：“士当以器识为先，一号为文人，无足观矣。”

gloss.en: 昭雪: to clear someone of a wrong.
gloss.zh: 昭雪：洗雪冤屈。

gloss.en: 形而上學, metaphysics: a modern translation word built on the Book of Changes, ‘what is above form is called the Way’.
gloss.zh: 形而上学：近代译名，取自《周易·系辞》“形而上者谓之道”。

gloss.en: 名學: logic, ‘the study of names’. 知識論: theory of knowledge.
gloss.zh: 名学：逻辑学。知识论：认识论。

gloss.en: 什佰: by tens and hundreds.
gloss.zh: 什佰：十个、百个。

gloss.en: 懲勸: punishing evil and encouraging good. 恉 is the same as 旨, purpose.
gloss.zh: 惩劝：惩恶劝善。恉：同“旨”，宗旨。

gloss.at: 而葸然以聽命於衆故也
gloss.at_hans: 而葸然以听命于众故也
gloss.en: 葸然: timidly.
gloss.zh: 葸然：畏缩的样子。

gloss.at: 胸中惝恍不可捉摸之意境
gloss.en: 惝恍: dim, vague, hard to hold.
gloss.zh: 惝恍：模糊不清、恍惚的样子。

gloss.at: 决非南面王之所能易者也
gloss.en: To sit facing south was the ruler’s place: a throne.
gloss.zh: 南面王：面南称王；古代君主坐北朝南。

gloss.en: 天職: a calling, the duty given by nature.
gloss.zh: 天职：天赋的职分。

marginalia.en: He places sacredness not in truth alone but in the friction, the moment it will not serve one country or one time. He was writing in 1905, when learning was widely expected to serve the rescue of the state.
marginalia.zh: 他把神圣放在了摩擦之处：真理不肯为一国一时所用的那一刻。他写这句话是在 1905 年，那时人们普遍期待学问为救国所用。

marginalia.at: 其有發明此真理（哲學家）
marginalia.en: The brackets are Wang’s own. He defines the philosopher and the artist in a single sentence, as servants of the same truth by different means: one discovers it, the other gives it signs.
marginalia.zh: 括号是王国维原有的。他在同一句话里定义了哲学家和美术家：二者服务于同一个真理，只是手段不同，一个发明它，一个用符号表现它。

marginalia.at: 其及於五世十世者希矣
marginalia.en: The argument rests on one thing that can be checked: how long a work goes on working. A library is where that check is made. Most texts on these shelves have outlasted the courts their authors served.
marginalia.zh: 这个论证只依赖一样可以检验的东西：一件作品能持续起作用多久。图书馆正是做这种检验的地方。这些书架上的大多数文字，都比它们的作者所侍奉的朝廷存在得更久。
